correctness.rationale: For the bipartite Levi graph of an existing projective plane of order q>=3, each edge-open packing induces a star forest and each selected edge determines one leaf. Orient components and put line leaves in X and point leaves in Y, whose opposite-type members must be nonincident. When both X and Y are nonempty, choose a leaf line L and leaf point y; letting Z be the off-L points lying on other X-lines yields q(|X|-1)<=q|Z|, while Y has at most q^2-|Z| points, so |B|=|X|+|Y|<=q^2+1<q(q+1). With one leaf side, two distinct centers have a joining line not itself available as a leaf, bounding |B| by q^2+q; equality forces that to be the sole missing line, every center on it and all other lines attached to the unique point of intersection. Dualize for the point version; there are exactly 2(q^2+q+1) distinct constructions and no others. Independent projective-coordinate incidence generation and maximal clique search at q=2,3 gave sizes 6,12 and exactly 14,26 maximizing edge sets, respectively, over 28 and 3094 inclusion-maximal cliques. The q>=3 theorem follows from the incidence proof and does not assert projective-plane existence for every integer q.
residual_risks: Enumeration is exhaustive only for q=2,3; other orders rest on the general projective-plane axioms.
No assertion is made that an arbitrary parameter q admits a projective plane, nor that q=2 shares the full theorem hypotheses.

value.rationale: The general |E|/delta degree bound equals q^2+q+1 on these regular incidence graphs, but the exact graph-specific optimum is one smaller and the entire equality set is rigidly controlled by a single omitted point or line. The classification and exact 2v count make the one-unit improvement structurally meaningful, not merely an isolated numerical gain. This is a natural infinite family including non-Desarguesian planes, and the incidence-counting mixed-leaf obstruction could be reusable.
residual_risks: The new scalar optimum differs by one from a general bound; mathematical interest depends on the proved rigidity and count rather than the gain itself.

limitations: No existence claim for arbitrary projective-plane order.
The q=2 Heawood case has a matching finite count but is outside the asserted q>=3 statement.
